evidence.observation: "Band 1 needs a new alethic row." Novelty is defined only per offending row (lines 164-166: "A violation key is `(address, canonical JSON of the offending row)`").

"decides the band from new rows only, and refuses to claim \"no new violations\" when either run is ill-formed or undecided (RC3)." Context: src/gnd/checker/_core.py:1032-1033 says "a ``cardinality`` ``min`` bound is genuinely decided — and violated — by a universe of zero". That is a fail with nothing to list. If base passes and head fails with zero rows, no new key appears and the run reports no new violations.
"survey every snapshot family's v7 offending-row shape and confirm each is values only." The survey checks row shape. It does not ask whether a family can fail with empty offending_facts.

concerns.recommendation: Also decide novelty at verdict level: an alethic verdict that is fail in head and not fail in base is new whatever its rows. Add 'can this family fail with no rows' to the family survey. Add an RC3 criterion: base passes and head fails a cardinality min bound with zero instances, and the run exits 1.
concerns.title: Deciding the band from new rows only lets a newly failing verdict with no offending rows read as 'no new violations'

evidence.observation: "Report versions 3-14 keep their bytes (rule 7)." But completion predicate 1 (lines 49-50) only claims "Version 7 bytes are unchanged for every existing input."

"Under version 15 only, a failing `acyclic` verdict's `offending_facts` lists every pair" while the home is "`src/gnd/checker/_core.py`, beside `_find_cycle`". evidence.observation: "Models with an active redaction policy or temporal terms re-project to versions 10/13 (`_project_result` in `src/gnd/checking_service.py`); `--rule-ids` refuses them in this milestone (RC1 D3)." "RC1-C4: `--rule-ids` with any other arm exits 64." That covers CLI arms only. A redaction policy is known only after the model loads, and the order "arguments (64), model load (3), head population load (3), base population load (3, naming the base), then evaluation" has no slot for this refusal.
"| Redacted values make a baseline key meaningless | `--rule-ids` (and so `--baseline`) refuses redaction-policy models |". This is the only control for that risk, and no criterion tests it.

concerns.recommendation: Add an RC1 criterion and an RC3 criterion: a redaction-policy model and a temporal model are each refused under --rule-ids and under --baseline, with a named exit code and a named place in the rule-3 order. Make clear whether 'RC1 D3' means the RC1 spec's D3.

evidence.observation: "exit 0, outcome `accepted`, `acceptance_ready: false`, counts show standing". Version 15 is "the version-7 snapshot shape" (line 142). evidence.observation: "Which cycle is named depends on traversal order, so two runs cannot be compared." Context: src/gnd/checker/_core.py:1377 already runs `_find_cycle(sorted(pair_set, key=repr))`, so for a given fact set the cycle is the same whatever the input order. What changes it is adding or removing an edge. The O5 probe (line 121) shows a single cycle, not order dependence.

"(791 and 18 on that project)" and "8 groups ... (sizes 90, 19, 13, 7, 3, 3, 2, 2)" are the requester's figures but are not marked claim, unlike O15. Rule 6 builds the synthetic fixture on "the 209-component data shape".

evidence.observation: "`gnd check MODEL HEAD --baseline BASE` (implies `--rule-ids`). Both populations are judged under MODEL."

"RC3-C4: key survives inserting a rule above another and inserting a fact above another." and RC-D4 "key by positional address, `addressing: positional` tells the caller it is unstable". Within one run, base and head share MODEL, so positional refs match and the rule-insertion half holds by construction. Across two models it is false for positional constraints, by RC-D4's own account.

Across models, the key is stable under rule insertion only for declared-id constraints, and a test shows positional keys move. Otherwise, name the stored artifact the cross-run claim is about.

"`--allow-vacuous` (run-wide) moves band 2 to 0 when vacuous verdicts are the only shortfall." response.summary: Draft r2 is well sourced. The O16/O17 reuse claims hold against address.py, coverage.py and model_index.py, every source issue (GR-D1, D2, D3, D5, D6) maps to a phase, and the RC1->RC2->RC3 sequencing is sound. Two blocking gaps: deciding the band from new rows only can miss a newly failing verdict that has no rows, and the frozen-variant claim (versions 3-14) is gated only on version 7 while RC2 changes a checker function that does not know the report version. The redaction refusal that protects baseline keys has no criterion. RC-D5 contradicts the acceptance_ready invariant. Several criteria cannot fail as written: time bounds without thresholds, RC2-C2, and RC3-C4's rule-insertion half.
